commercial_engagement_definition.publisher_definition: Coinbase defines commercial engagement broadly to include financial or business activities involving the asset, its issuer or an affiliated party; the engagement may have begun before or after Coinbase supported the asset.
commercial_engagement_definition.interpretation: A Yes flag is evidence of a Coinbase-reported commercial relationship under its broad definition, not proof of a direct Ripple agreement, XRP purchase, collateral posting or a specific payment rail.

interpretation.supported: Coinbase's disclosure marks XRP as held and commercially engaged in its US trading-assets table and its Coinbase Custody Trust Company table; the custody table also marks cbXRP Yes/Yes and RLUSD No/Yes.
interpretation.vintage_limit: The page states Coinbase holding data are as of 2026-03-31. Do not present the holding flags as November 8 balances.
interpretation.relationship_limit: Commercial engagement is broad and can involve the asset, issuer or affiliate; the page does not identify Ripple as the specific counterparty.
interpretation.capital_limit: No quantity, dollar balance, customer custody balance, XRP collateral balance, purchase flow or net capital amount is disclosed.
counter_hypotheses: The engagement flag may relate to custody, listing, an affiliate or another business/financial activity rather than direct issuer financing.
The March 31 holding vintage may not reflect holdings on the November 8 page crawl date.
A Yes holding flag does not quantify balance or establish whether the holding is corporate inventory versus customer assets.
interpretation.source_independence: Single Coinbase primary disclosure; no independent confirmation.
